grammar.label: passive infinitive and passive gerund
grammar.form: to be + past participle; being + past participle; to have been + past participle
grammar.meaning: the subject receives the action inside a non-finite clause

explanation.en: A non-finite verb has a passive too: 'The form needs to be signed', 'She hates being interrupted', 'He claims to have been misled'. Choose the passive when the doer is unknown, obvious, or deliberately left out.
explanation.uz: Noaniq shakldagi fe'lning ham majhul nisbati bor: 'The form needs to be signed', 'She hates being interrupted'. Bajaruvchi noma'lum yoki ataylab aytilmagan bo'lsa, majhul nisbat tanlanadi.

grammar.positive_example: Nobody likes being told what to do.
grammar.negative_example: Nobody likes be told what to do.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida majhul nisbat qo'shimcha bilan yasaladi, ingliz tilida esa 'be' + III shakl zanjirini to'liq qurish kerak; 'be' tushib qolishi eng keng tarqalgan xato.

grammar.label: the get-passive and its register
grammar.meaning: the same event as a be-passive, but spoken, sudden, or unwelcome

explanation.en: 'He got fired' and 'He was fired' describe one event in two registers: 'get' is spoken, dynamic, and usually carries misfortune or a sudden change. It is rare in formal writing and never used with state verbs — 'The house is owned by my aunt', not 'gets owned'.
explanation.uz: 'He got fired' va 'He was fired' — bitta voqea, ikki uslub: 'get' og'zaki, keskin va ko'pincha noxush ma'no beradi. Rasmiy yozuvda kam qo'llanadi va holat fe'llari bilan ishlatilmaydi.

grammar.positive_example: Their car got stolen outside the station.
grammar.negative_example: The house gets owned by my aunt.

l1_notes.uz: Uslubiy farq: rasmiy xatda 'get'-majhul nisbatini ishlatmaslik kerak.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The letter needs to be written again. It reads like a punishment.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Staff who fail to comply will face action.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Nobody likes being told they will be punished before they have done anything.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: So what do I write instead?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: 'The form must be signed before the first of each month.' Same rule, no threat.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And if somebody asks what happens when it is not?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then you tell them. You do not print it at the top.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Bobur says a colleague of his got dismissed over a form like this.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: 'Got dismissed' is how he tells it in a corridor. In the letter it is 'was dismissed'.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Does the register really matter that much?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: The facts are the same. Which one you choose tells the reader how you see them.
